note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the first full build, starting from a brief for a lionfish drawn in a super-geometric style.
note.changing: First full build: a side-on lionfish with crimson and cream ring stripes and a jewel eye, a mandala of eye-shaped petals and string-art stars behind it, cube-tiled corners, and the name SAVESFISH on a stepped temple band at the bottom.
note.why: The lionfish's spines already look like rays of light, so letting them literally become the rays of a sacred-geometry burst ties the animal and the hyperspace together.
note.idea: A side-on lionfish whose 13 dorsal spines radiate exactly from the centre of the badge, so its crown of venomous needles doubles as the starburst of a mandala, with op-art ring stripes on the body, a jewel eye, string-art star polygons and stepped Mayan temple geometry behind it, and the name on a temple band at the bottom.

note.saw: The spines looked like thick bamboo sticks, the background petals were big, flat and empty, and the ring of glyphs around the rim was sparse.
note.changing: Fills the background with a faceted chrysanthemum of jewel kites, a spiralling hex tunnel and rainbow string art, gives the fins op-art ring membranes, and covers the body in tiny hex scales.
note.why: DMT space is made of jewels and lattices; flat shapes read as clip art.

note.saw: The crown got lost as a pink collar; colours flat, eyes too tiny.
note.changing: Rainbow contour echoes around the whole fish, a cyan neon edge on every spine, longer spines with diamond tips, big faceted eyes in the kites, Mayan square-spiral frets on the temple.
note.why: Outline-gap-outline rainbow bands (reference 1) make the hero glow off the busy background.

note.saw: The pectoral fan looked like a scallop shell.
note.changing: Op-art sector checkerboard in the fins, glowing cyan halo, a 240-tick dial ring, sparkles.
note.why: Shifting alternate sectors by half a band makes the fin shimmer like op-art instead of reading as a shell.

note.saw: One motif (the kite) repeated 72 times; Mayan steps only at the bottom.
note.changing: Stepped ziggurat rays in the back ring, crisp jewel cells in the hex tunnel, fang-like chin tabs removed.
note.why: Mixing eye-petals with temple steps brings in the stepped jewel geometry of reference 3.

note.saw: The background was one motif, the eye-kite, repeated 72 times, and the stepped Mayan geometry only appeared at the bottom.
note.changing: Swaps the outer ring of blue kites for dark stepped staircase towers that radiate out from the centre behind the remaining eye-petals.
note.why: Mixing eye-petals with temple steps breaks the repetition and carries the Mayan stepped geometry all the way around the mandala.

note.saw: Wanted entities and the fluffy lionfish "mane".
note.changing: Tried entity faces in the kites and a far-side pectoral fan.
note.why: Experiment: faces turned the kites into tiny arrowheads, so they were reverted next round.

note.saw: The new staircase towers were still plain dark shapes, the pectoral rays read as black tubes, and the chin tabs looked like vampire fangs.
note.changing: Gives the towers gold and magenta inset echoes with dotted borders, fills the hex tunnel with crisp jewel cells glowing from gold to magenta to ultraviolet, tones down the core glow, widens the fin rays and removes the fang-like tabs.
note.why: Mixing eye-petals with jewelled temple steps brings in the stepped jewel geometry of the reference art, and crisp cells read better than blurred haze.

note.saw: Faces too small to read; the far fin poked under the tail.
note.changing: Back to big single eye-petals with a third-eye jewel; far pectoral shortened; neon lettering rim.
note.why: One big readable eye beats three unreadable ones.

note.saw: The eye-kites were only single eyes, with no real entities yet, and the lionfish still lacked its fluffy 'mane' of two overlapping pectoral fans.
note.changing: Tries entity faces in the front kites (two slanted almond eyes, a third-eye jewel and a mouth) and adds a second pectoral fan on the far side of the body.
note.why: An experiment: faces would make the mandala feel inhabited, and a second fan behind the first would give the lionfish its full, fluffy look.

note.saw: The owner asked for a much more legible name (cap height 44+, calm backing).
note.changing: Rebuilt the name as big split caps SAVES · FISH on a stepped Mayan arc cartouche with a calm dark interior.
note.why: The name has to read instantly at badge size; a calm dark band keeps the busy art off the letters.

note.saw: The faces were too small to read and turned the kites into tiny arrowheads, and the far fin's rays poked out under the tail.
note.changing: Goes back to big single eye-petals with a third-eye jewel above each, and shortens and lowers the far fin so it just peeks out between the near fan and the anal fin.
note.why: One big readable eye beats three unreadable ones, and the shorter far fin keeps the mane without spiking the tail.

note.saw: The big eye-petals were back and working; the name and the jewel eye were now the only key parts without any neon of their own.
note.changing: Gives the lettering a neon cyan rim behind its magenta extrusion and a dotted cream marquee inlay, and rings the jewel eye with a cyan glow.
note.why: A neon rim lifts the name and the eye off the busy pattern, so both read at a glance even at badge size.

note.saw: SavesFish asked for a much more legible name; at 240 pixels the old SAVESFISH lettering was readable but too small.
note.changing: Rebuilds the name as big split capitals, SAVES and FISH with a faceted jewel between them, along a bottom arc inside a stepped Mayan cartouche with a calm dark interior: solid cream letters over magenta, ink and a glowing cyan rim, with no 3D extrusion. The old straight band and temple tiers are gone, and the fin rays now stop short of the letters.
note.why: The name has to read instantly at badge size; a calm dark band keeps the busy art off the letters.

note.saw: The second artist picks up the first artist's finished piece, after SavesFish said it needed to be a lot better.
note.changing: Nothing changes yet: this is the first artist's final, rendered again exactly as it was so it could be studied with fresh eyes.
note.why: Before rebuilding anything, the second artist looked hard at the full render, the badge, a 160-pixel thumbnail and close-up zooms to find the six biggest weaknesses.
note.idea: Rebuild the fish from real lionfish anatomy (a big head with two banded tentacles over the eye, 13 needle spines radiating from the badge centre with pennant flags, a huge feathery pectoral wing, spotted soft fins, bands that straighten toward the tail and a spiral vortex for a face) and light it from behind with a true hyperspace: a tunnel of jewel cells pulling into a white-gold core, a chrysanthemum of eye petals, temple towers and a dense Mayan glyph frieze.

note.saw: The tunnel spilled past the rim into the corners as big dark hexagons, flat magenta petals fought the crimson fish, glowing halos fused the spines into a solid wall, and the cheek tabs looked like fangs.
note.changing: Keeps the tunnel inside the disc with finer cells, adds flower-of-life circle webs and cooler faceted petals, thins the halos and takes the flags out of them, removes the fang tabs, and edges the gill cover in gold with a cyan diamond chain.
note.why: A crown of venomous needles has to read as separate needles; a wall of halo hides the very thing that makes a lionfish a lionfish.

note.saw: The crown now read as 13 separate banded needles, but the background was a monotone blue-violet ring and still had no light.
note.changing: Rebuilds the petals and stepped temple towers in full-spectrum bands (cyan, emerald, yellow, orange, magenta and violet, with dark gaps between), sets a warm blurred backlight aura behind the fish, and redraws the face as twisted bands with tiny eyes.
note.why: Rainbow contour bands and jewel steps come straight from the reference art, and the aura makes the fish look lit from the core of the portal behind it: the moment the piece started to glow.

note.saw: The soft fins and the far pectoral looked like seashells glued on, the mouth was two thin lines, and the eye ring looked like a monocle.
note.changing: Rebuilds the soft dorsal and anal fins as rows of near-parallel spotted rays, removes the far pectoral, and gives the fish a gold-lipped mouth, a tight eye ring and mirrored sparkles around the crown.
note.why: Real lionfish soft fins are clear membranes with rows of dark spots, not radial fans.

note.saw: The wing's free rays sat inside heavy black lobes, leaving a dark skirt under the fish.
note.changing: Gives the pectoral wing its own thin neon edge, kept off the body, darkens the outer ring toward the frieze for depth, adds tiny lionfish glyphs to the Mayan frieze, and runs diamond chains down the pale face bands.
note.why: The feathery rays should float over the light, and the fish now repeats at three scales (the hero, the frieze glyphs and the fish-shaped eye petals): self-similar, like a real trip.

note.saw: The wing membrane looked like a messy weave, and the rays met in a dark hole at the fin root.
note.changing: Redraws the wing in crisp op-art sector bands, sets a faceted gold and crimson rosette with a jewel where the rays meet, and puts big spiral eyes at both ends of the name band.
note.why: Clean geometry over noise: this piece is 'super geometric', so every pattern should look ruled and exact.

note.saw: At about 400 pixels wide the crown of spines melted into the warm petals behind it, so the starburst lost its punch.
note.changing: Makes the spines bolder with a stronger cyan edge, gives the petals cool rims around warm glowing cores, and enlarges the eye portal.
note.why: Warm needles read best against cool light, and the starburst is the piece's big idea, so it has to punch.

note.saw: Round 15 worked: the crown punched, the wing floated and the name read at 240 pixels. The Visionary noticed the needle tips simply stopping at the frieze, and the corner cubes sitting still 'like they haven't noticed the portal'.
note.changing: Rings thin cyan and magenta ripples around every needle tip, makes the corner cubes shrink and dim toward the rim with a tiny watching eye on every few, and sets a gold twelve-pointed star in the eye's iris.
note.why: The ripples turn thirteen sticks into thirteen antennae touching hyperspace, and the shrinking, watching cubes make the whole room fall into the badge instead of being wallpaper.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's needle-tip ripples and its shrinking, watching corner cubes, but turned down its fin-root gem because a crimson-and-gold jewel rosette already sat there.

note.saw: The needle-tip ripples worked, but the shrinking cubes left the corners full of dark gaps: floating cubes in a void, which broke the rule of no empty corners.
note.changing: Rebuilds the corners as a cube tunnel: rings of 72 tightly packed cubes that shrink as they fall toward the rim, each turned so its top points away from the portal, with tiny eyes on some of the top faces.
note.why: It is the same trick as the hex tunnel inside the badge, applied outside it: the whole square becomes one vortex of geometry pouring into the lionfish portal, with no empty space anywhere.
note.visionary: Keeps the Visionary's idea of corners falling toward the portal, but rebuilds it as a packed tunnel so no gaps open up.

note.saw: The cube corners worked, but in a 4x close-up the tail and soft fins were partly see-through, so the busy petals showed through and the tail went muddy.
note.changing: Gives the tail, soft dorsal and anal fins a solid deep-indigo base under their pale veil, with the crimson spot arcs, rays and spots on top.
note.why: In a super-geometric piece every shape should be crisp; a dark stained-glass base lets the spot rows and rays glow instead of mixing with the background.

note.saw: The deep-indigo fin bases were crisp up close but turned the tail and soft fins a dull, heavy mauve at badge size: the fish lost a third of its glow.
note.changing: Puts the tail, soft dorsal and anal fins on a solid pale rose base with a faint magenta veil, so the crimson arcs, ray lines and maroon spots read like a lionfish's clear spotted fins, but solid.
note.why: Crisp and bright at once: the whole fish now glows pale against the dark contour bands, and at 160 pixels the rounded spotted tail reads instantly.

visions.seen: The lionfish is a crowned priest burning in a cathedral of eye-petals, all thirteen needles humming like tuning forks, and the backlight is pouring through it from the core. But under its wing there is a little black drain where the rays meet, and the light leaks away there. The cube wallpaper in the corners just sits still, like it hasn't noticed the portal yet.
suggestions: The pectoral fin root, just behind the gill cover at the centre-left of the body (about x 330, y 395 in the 800 render), where the feathery rays meet in a dark hole and the moire weave goes muddy: I see a small faceted jewel there, about 20 px across. A dark centre, then a ring of 12 alternating gold and cyan triangle facets, then a thin cyan neon edge. Keep it a gem, not a second eye, so the real eye stays in charge. Inside the inner quarter of the membrane, around the jewel, the weave could give way to rings of tiny cream beads on crimson that get bigger as they move outward. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace every place where lines meet is a node that throws out light. The wing would bloom out of a lit seed instead of sliding into a drain, and the gem would echo the jewel-portal eye.

The thirteen crown needle tips, top of the disc (y about 100 to 140), where they reach the frieze ring: I see each tip breaking through a skin. Two or three thin concentric arcs around each tip (cyan, then magenta, opacity going 0.7 to 0.3 outward, radii about 4, 7 and 10 px), as if the needle is piercing the membrane of the world and making ripples. Clip the ripples so they stay inside the frieze's inner edge. Why it's more DMT: the breakthrough feels like poking through a film into the next room. The crown stops being a fan of sticks and becomes thirteen antennae touching the edge of hyperspace.

The four corner cube fields outside the rim: let the lattice feel the pull of the portal. Shrink the cubes as they get close to the rim (full size in the far corners, down to about 55% where they touch the merlon edge) and dim the far-corner cubes a little, so the badge reads as a hole the whole room is falling into. On about every 7th cube, swap the inner diamond of the top face for a tiny almond eye (cream white, dark pupil), the same eye-language as the petals. Why it's more DMT: the walls of the DMT room are made of tiles that watch you and lean toward the centre. Right now the corners are a calm floor; this would make them part of the vortex.
visions.keep: The neon SAVES·FISH split capitals with the jewel dot, on their calm dark stepped band (they read at 240 px; leave every letter and that band alone). The thirteen banded needles with eye-petals glowing between them. The full-spectrum chrysanthemum of eye-petals and temple towers. The warm backlight aura behind the fish. The spiral face vortex and the jewel-portal eye. The tiny lionfish glyphs in the frieze (the fish at three scales). The spotted tail with its echo bands. The new delicate thin neon edge on the pectoral that lets the free rays float over the petals.

visions.seen: The corners finally woke up: the whole square is a carpet of tumbling dice pouring into the lionfish, and the needle tips really are pricking the skin of the world now, little rings humming on every spine. But the dice are confetti, every cube a random colour, so I feel the tunnel in the geometry and then lose it in the noise, and every eye in the room is staring straight ahead at nothing.
suggestions: The four corner cube fields outside the rim (the log-polar tunnel from round 17): I see the colour ordered instead of scattered. Give each cube its hue from the petals' own six-band spectrum (cyan, emerald, yellow, orange, magenta, violet) with `palette[(i + k) % 6]`, where i is the cube's index around its ring of 72 and k is the ring number. That one line turns the confetti into twelve rainbow spiral arms all leaning the same way, staircasing down into the merlon edge. If you want them to really turn, rotate each ring about 2.5° more than the one outside it, so the arms bend into true log spirals. Keep the tight packing, the three-face shading and the tiny eyes. Why it's more DMT: hyperspace is never random, it is impossibly ordered, and the order moves. Ordered colour lets the eye ride the vortex down into the badge, and it calms the corners so the disc stays the jewel.

Every almond eye in the room: the eye petals of the chrysanthemum all around the fish (the big ones left of the snout, about x 60 to 200, y 250 to 470 in the 800 render, and the yellow-green ones between the lower fin rays) plus the tiny eyes on the corner cubes. I see their pupils all turning to the same point. Slide each iris and pupil off-centre toward the lionfish's jewel-portal eye (about x 248, y 327 in the 800 render, 124, 164 in the 400 box) by about 30% of the almond's half-width: work out the direction in page coordinates, rotate it into each petal's own frame, and clamp so the iris stays inside the almond. The cube eyes can look at the badge centre (200, 200) instead. Why it's more DMT: the breakthrough is the moment every eye in the room turns and looks at the same thing at once. A converging gaze field is ruled radial geometry, and it hands all that attention to the fish's eye, so the hero eye gets louder without getting bigger.

The frieze tile ring between the disc and the merlon edge: the glyphs now come in short repeated runs (I I I, + +, triangle triangle), mirrored left and right. I see one glyph shapeshifting around the ring like a filmstrip. Going clockwise from the top-centre tile, the square spiral loses one turn per tile, straightens into the zigzag, closes into the triangle, grows an iris into the eye, sprouts three spines and becomes the little lionfish glyph; the next stretch plays it backwards. Draw every frame on the same 5x5 stroke grid with the same number of polyline points and just interpolate the points between keyframes, so it stays ruled and exact. Keep the tile shapes and colours. Why it's more DMT: the elves don't talk, they show you glyphs that transform while you watch, and here the language spells out the lionfish all the way around the portal.
visions.keep: The neon SAVES·FISH split capitals with the jewel dot on their calm dark stepped band (they read at 240 px; leave every letter and that band alone). The thirteen banded crown needles and the ripple rings at their tips (so glad those took). The tightly packed cube tunnel with its tiny eyes and no empty corners. The jewel-portal eye with its gold {12/5} star, the spiral face vortex, the faceted rosette at the fin root, the crisp op-art wing, the full-spectrum eye petals and temple towers, the warm backlight aura, the spotted tail with its echo bands, and the lionfish at three scales.

visions.seen: The tail went from bruised plum to pale rose and the whole fish lit up like a paper lantern. The fins breathe light now instead of swallowing it. But the body stripes stand at attention like fence posts while the eye beside them is a whirlpool: the portal pulls at the whole room except its own body.
suggestions: The crimson and cream body stripes, from the gill chain to the tail root (about x 330 to 600, y 250 to 470 in the 800 render; x 165 to 300 in the 400 box): I see them as wavefronts poured out of the jewel-portal eye. Instead of straight vertical bands, each stripe could be a ring centred on the eye (about 248, 327 in the 800 render; 124, 164 in the 400 box), clipped to the body path. Keep the band count, the sawtooth edges and the little diamond eyes riding each cream band. Let each ring be about 4% wider than the one inside it, so the ripple spreads as it travels. If the first rings curl too tightly behind the gill, slide the centre left toward the snout (about x 150 in the 800 render) until they flatten into gentle bows. Why it's more DMT: the face spiral gives you the angles and the rings give you the radii, so face and body lock into one polar field and the whole fish becomes a broadcast from its own eye. It echoes the ripples at the needle tips, and real lionfish stripes curve anyway.

The three pale rose fans (the tail on the right, the soft dorsal above the tail root, the anal fin below it): keep round 19's opaque pale base exactly. I just see the crimson arcs bunching toward the scalloped edge. Make each arc band about 0.82 of the width of the one inside it, and let the maroon spots shrink about 10% per ring outward, so each fan bulges like a fisheye dome and the scallop becomes a horizon curving away. Why it's more DMT: in hyperspace flat things turn out to be lenses. The fins stay calm and glowing at badge size, but up close they bend space instead of lying flat on it.

The white four-point sparkles scattered through the dark lattice around the fish (left of the snout about x 110 to 220, y 380 to 520, and right of the tail about x 590 to 680, y 360 to 480): I see light breaking into its spectrum. Give each sparkle a 1 px cyan copy offset up-left and a 1 px magenta copy offset down-right (prism fringe), add short diagonal rays to make an 8-point flare, and snap each one onto the nearest vertex of the thin background lattice so they sit on the grid like charged nodes. Why it's more DMT: they are the only light in the room that is still plain white. DMT light is always prismatic, and the flares become part of the lattice's geometry instead of glitter dropped on it.
visions.keep: Round 19's pale rose fins: the fish finally glows end to end and the rounded spotted tail reads at 160 px. The neon SAVES·FISH split capitals with the jewel dot on their calm dark stepped band (leave every letter and that band alone). The jewel-portal eye with its gold {12/5} star, the spiral face vortex, the cyan and gold gill chain, the faceted fin-root rosette, the crisp op-art wing, the thirteen banded needles with their tip ripples, the tightly packed cube tunnel, the full-spectrum eye petals and temple towers, the warm backlight aura, and the lionfish at three scales.
